tara: Hey team — GlacierFin just asked for a Dedicated batching/queue config that keeps their p95 output latency under 400ms while staying inside a 30% cost uplift. Can ops propose a per-customer queue/token ceiling we can try? :eyes:

yusuf: Quick context — their production trace shows large fan-in of short chat messages (avg 18 tokens) plus occasional long completions (1k+ tokens) for statements. Our continuous batching currently builds batches up to 64 requests or 4s timeout.

celine: From profiling yesterday, kernel selection flips to slower matmul path for sequence lengths >1024 which killed throughput. We should avoid forcing long requests into the same batch with many short ones.

yusuf: Agreed. Proposal: soft_token_ceiling=12000 per queue, max_batch_size=48, max_concurrent_batches=6, long_request_cutoff=512 tokens (route to separate long-req lane). That should reduce head-of-line blocking.

tara: Can you show the config snippet you'd apply on Dedicated for GlacierFin? Also need queue token budget per GPU pool and fallback policy.

yusuf: Snippet below (will apply via dedicated config):

```
queues:
  - name: glacierfin-default
    soft_token_ceiling: 12000
    max_batch_size: 48
    max_concurrent_batches: 6
    long_request_cutoff: 512
    prioritize_short_requests: true
fallback:
  on_capacity_exhausted: route_to: glacierfin-spot (lower-cost quantized models)
  on_latency_degradation: reduce_soft_ceiling: 8000
```

celine: Based on the profiler: with a 12k token ceiling we simulated 18% better tokens/sec and p95 stayed ~370ms under steady load. But under a 20% spike long-tail p95 jumps ~200ms if long reqs mix in. Separating long_request_cutoff lane keeps that extra tail to ~80ms.

evan-cs: GlacierFin asks for a hard SLA at 450ms p95. Are we comfortable shipping soft ceilings only, or do they want strict hard ceilings with rejection?

tara: Customer prefers graceful degradation, not hard rejects. They accept reroutes to quantized model pool and increased cost budgeting for peak. We'll present canary with metrics.

infra-bot: deploy plan created: <https://internal.redwood/deploys/PR-5123|PR-5123> — canary 5% traffic to glacierfin-default on pool-prod-3, start 0300 UTC tomorrow.

yusuf: Ops runbook note: monitor these signals during canary: per-queue p95 latency, queue length, avg batch size, tokens_per_batch, kernel_switch_rate (seq>1024). If kernel_switch_rate > 5% for a sustained minute, trigger auto-fallback.

tara: Also add KV cache note — enable aggressive prefix caching for short-chat paths (TTL 60s). This should reduce repeated context decoding and free up token budget. Caching needs to be per-customer, per-model.

celine: I'll update the performance dashboard to show 'glacierfin-default' lane metrics and add a regression alert if p95 > 420ms or tokens/sec drops 15% vs baseline.

evan-cs: I'll tell GlacierFin CS team about the canary and expected behavior: soft ceilings + reroute to quantized on spikes.

tara: Thanks. After canary (48h), we'll collect traces and decide whether to tighten long_request_cutoff or reduce soft_ceiling. :thumbsup:
